summary: Reginald Heber worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Brasenose College and the University of Oxford, receiving an M.A. and a D.D., and served as a Fellow at All Souls College, Oxford, beginning in 1805.

Reginald Stephen Copleston was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Merton College and Exeter College, Oxford, served as a Fellow at St John's College, Oxford (1870–1875), and was President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1876–1902).
Rei Yoshimura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He was educated at Waseda University, where he later served as a professor from circa 1974 to 2000.
Reiho Masunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Kaiten Nukariya from circa 1925 to 1931. He served as a teacher at Komazawa University from circa 1930 to 1972.

Reiko Ohnuma specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez and Padmanabh S. Jaini. Her posts include visiting lecturer at UT Austin, and positions at the University of Alabama and Dartmouth College.

Reimon Yuki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Daijō Tokiwa at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Academy of Oriental Culture, the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, Kyoto Women's University, and Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Dendo-in.

Reiner Wiehl was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Nancy and Goethe University Frankfurt. He served as Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and Heidelberg University (appointed 1977).

Reinhold F. G. Müller worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the universities of Berlin, Innsbruck, and Greifswald, where he served as an assistant (~1909–1911), later becoming a Privatdozent in medicine at the University of Leipzig in 1942.

Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indologist who worked in Indology at Göttingen State and University Library (attested 1994–2008). He has also held posts at Free University of Berlin, University of Trento, Paris Descartes University, University of Oxford, and Ohio University.

Reinhold Klotz worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He completed his habilitation at the University of Leipzig, where he served as assistant professor from 1832 and as außerordentlicher Professor from 1849 until 1870, succeeding Gottfried Hermann.

Reinhold Niebuhr was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Elmhurst University, Eden Theological Seminary, and Yale Divinity School, and served on the faculty at Union Theological Seminary from circa 1928 to 1960.

Reinhold Rost was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Johann Gildemeister and Johann Gustav Stickel at the University of Jena. He held posts at St Augustine's College, the Royal Asiatic Society, King's College London, and the India Office.

Reinhold Trautmann specialized in linguistics. After studies under Friedrich Kluge, Wilhelm Schulze, Adalbert Bezzenberger, and Jacob Wackernagel, he held professorships at Prague, Königsberg, and Leipzig, followed by a chair at Jena and heading the Academy of Sciences of the GDR.

Reinhold von Stackelberg specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Tartu, Leipzig, and Strasbourg, and held posts as Privatdozent at the University of Leipzig (1891–1892) and Professor of Persian at the Lazarev Institute (1894).
Reirin Yamada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and served as president of Komazawa Junior College.
Rembert Lutjeharms is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Oxford by 2010 and held a post at the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies (attested 2016–2026).
Remeen Firoz is an Indologist who is a PhD student at the Australian National University under the supervision of Assa Doron (attested 2026).
Rena Aronovna Aulova was an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied at the National University of Uzbekistan from circa 1944 to 1949 and was appointed a docent there in 1979.

Renate Syed is an Indologist who studied at the University of Munich (~1974–1982) under Dieter Schlingloff, Friedrich Wilhelm, and Gritli von Mitterwallner. She is attested as a Privatdozentin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Renato Dávalos is an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at UAM, UNAM, El Colegio de México, and the University of Cologne. He served as a researcher fellow at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique from 2023 to 2026.
